newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers attack Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers attack Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Jewish settlers attacked three Palestinians before exchanging blows with Israeli police in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday, witnesses said.
Witnesses said a group of some 50 Jewish youths assaulted the Palestinians shortly after nightfall in Hebron, punching and hitting their arms and bodies.
"The settlers beat my brother and then he was arrested," Muhammad al-Heih told Reuters.

Witnesses said some of the settlers exchanged blows with Israeli paramilitary police who arrived at the scene to break up the incident. Israeli police and soldiers fanned out in Hebron to disperse Arabs and Jews in the city centre.
"At present, five local residents and three Jewish youth have been brought in for questioning," a police spokesman said.
He said the Jews were being questioned on the assault and that the Palestinians were being interrogated on claims they had attacked Jewish women.

"Initial checks indicate that the background for the confrontation seems to be a number of recent occasions...(when) Jewish girls passed by and local residents attacked them, cursed them and made obscene gestures," the spokesman said.
About 400 Jewish settlers live and study in heavily armed compounds in the heart of Hebron, a volatile city of 100,000 Arabs holy to both Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

In 1994, Baruch Goldstein, an American-born Jewish militant from the nearby settlement of Kiryat Arba, gunned down 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer in Hebron's Tomb of the Patriarchs, called al-Haram al-Ibrahimi by Moslems.
Hebron is now the focus of stalemated Israeli-PLO talks on an overdue Israeli troop redeployment in the city.

Israeli troops were due to have turned over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule under a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation. The pullback was delayed after a wave of Islamic militant suicide bombings killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
